sourceAnchors.message: Ensure that resources like this ExecutorService object are closed after use
sourceAnchors.reason: Exact standalone JUnit shared-service8-worker64-call negative-leak test. Every task creates its own memory-only JDBC Port, password array, row lists and fault map. Shared service returns ALREADY_EXISTS before password hashing/inserts/audits, verified by exact first4 SQL and wiped private input. Every Future has5-second get and finally shutdownNow with asserted10-second awaitTermination. No container/application thread or actual database/resource authority is created.

sourceAnchors.message: Avoid using equals() to compare against null
sourceAnchors.reason: Intentional independent negative equals(null)==false assertion for generated record contracts, not an application null test. Replacing it with reference comparison would stop executing/verifying the record method and miss the specified null behavior. Both return and absence of an exception are observed; no production null handling or exception is suppressed.

sourceAnchors.message: Use equals() to compare object references.
sourceAnchors.reason: This exact JDBC dynamic-proxy Object.equals implementation deliberately implements identity equality. Calling proxy.equals recursively re-enters the same InvocationHandler and never terminates. The compared reference is the proxy itself; no domain value comparison occurs. The memory-only fixture needs identity, not application equality semantics.

sourceAnchors.sourceAnchor: final Map<String, Throwable> faults = new HashMap<>();
sourceAnchors.message: If you run in Java5 or newer and have concurrent access, you should use the ConcurrentHashMap implementation
sourceAnchors.reason: Per-Port private fault configuration; every sequential test and each concurrent task creates a separate Port. No Port/fault map is static, published or shared across tasks; mutation precedes the same-thread service call. Concurrent test shares only the service and immutable metadata, never a Port. ConcurrentHashMap would add no required thread-safety contract.

sourceAnchors.message: In J2EE, getClassLoader() might not work as expected.  Use Thread.currentThread().getContextClassLoader() instead.
sourceAnchors.reason: Standalone JUnit memory-only JDBC dynamic proxy, not J2EE code. This exact loader owns the fixed java.sql interface and establishes its visibility for Proxy.newProxyInstance. No application/plugin interface, context loader selection, service lookup or deployment occurs; using a mutable Thread context loader would introduce unrelated ambient state. All4 interfaces use the same explicit interface-owned loader policy.
